_comment: llama_attnres (cell X) build receipt, 24 Oct 2026: arch.custom.attn_res {form full, scale sources|none} on the llama block, ops::depth_attend fused (host + CUDA kernels), IR family llama_attnres, ember gate files. Numbers from tests/test_llama_attnres.cpp and tests/test_llama_attnres_ir.py on the laptop's CPU; CUDA compiled and linked only (validation on Colab: tools/colab_cuda_validate.sh leg test_llama_attnres).

init_equivalence._note: zero pseudo-queries against the plain llama of the same seed (identical non-query tensors bit for bit). scale sources: every sublayer input is S * mean of the sources = the plain stream to rounding; scale none (Kimi's convex mixture): rmsnorm(x / S) = x / sqrt(mean x^2 + S^2 eps), eps 1e-5, which at the default init (stream mean square ~4e-4, S up to 33) shrinks deep sublayer inputs and the head.
init_equivalence.why_not_bit_equal: a_i = fl(1/S) and the mixture sums S rounded products before the S rescale, against the plain model's sequential adds: equal to rounding (exact when S is a power of two)

cpu_throughput_20m_L16._note: mtstudio run, T 256, batch 2, 2 cores (cpu_budget), steps 3-12, laptop shared with other jobs: attnres and attnres_none do identical work, so their spread (1.02 vs 0.85) is contention noise; the depth attention is ~1.5% of a step's FLOPs and not resolvable on CPU.

gpu_estimate_20m_L16_L4._note: bandwidth estimate, not a measurement: the fused kernels read every source twice forward and twice backward and write one gradient per source per call (sum of S over a model = 560 at L16), plus the tape's accumulation of those gradients: about 80 GB per 16,384-token step, ~0.3-0.4 s on an L4, on top of plain's 0.645 s/step (E1 probe_20m_L16, 25,383 tok/s). Expected X/P16 ~0.6-0.7, against the 0.3 costed in PREREGISTRATION_DRAFT section 10. The composed tape form would be far slower on the device (ops::mul_row and ops::scale are host-only: a round trip per source). Measured by tools/colab_chat/tiny_chat_long_x_probe.json.
